raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview The 2D unified attention kernel prefills with `BLOCK_M=16`, so each program covers only `16 // num_queries_per_kv` query positions and KV tiles are re-read many times. This uses a 64/128-row tile for prefill-heavy batches on sm80/sm89. gpt-oss always runs this kernel there (FA2 and FlashInfer can't do sinks on those GPUs). Related: #20690 (same idea, closed as stale), #52684 (same technique on ROCm), #60317 (head_dim 256/512 tuning, same launch code), #37949 (draft, KV tile for sink prefill on SM8x), #59878 (would move gpt-oss on SM8x to FlashInfer). ## Claims - gpt-oss-20b and Qwen3-8B on A100: TTFT of a long prompt −9 % (4k) to −32 % (32k), throughput up to +43 %. Under open-loop mixed load TTFT and TPOT are lower than main in all four workloads I ran. - Prefill kernel 1.95x (A100) / 2.17x (L4) geomean on batches of 2048+ tokens where the tile is used. - Not bitwise identical to main. bf16 greedy outputs change, and the RMS logprob error against fp32 is about 4 % higher than main's. Top-1 accuracy is not significantly different. ## Validation A100-SXM4-40GB and L4 (Colab), vLLM wheel `0.32.1rc1.dev481+gb3466364b` with the changed files copied in (the base versions of both files equal upstream `6674eedd2`), torch 2.14.0+cu130, triton 3.8.0. Benchmark scripts and raw data are kept locally; I can post them if useful. The sweep, closed-loop and numerics runs used an earlier revision of the gate (sm12x allowed, no token floor in the closed-loop runs); for the measured shapes the final gate picks the same batches. Saturated, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` and test runs used the final code (the last commit only changes comments and docstrings). Tests (L4 is the CI GPU for these tests; sm80 isn't in CI): ```bash pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py -k "prefill_block_m or prefill_tile" pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py ``` | GPU | `-k` selection | whole file | |---|---|---| | L4 | 13 passed | 1930 passed | | A100 | 12 passed, 1 skipped (fp8 output needs sm89) | not run | The tests check the launched `BLOCK_M`/`num_warps` with and without opting in, compare against a reference with sinks (sliding window, softcap, fp16, GQA 5/7/12, head 80/96, Gemma-3-like shape), and check that ALiBi, non-causal and fp8-output calls keep the default tile. Kernel, tile on vs off, 570 batches per GPU, batches of 2048+ tokens where the tile is used: | GPU | batches | geomean | worst | |---|---|---|---| | A100 | 184 | 1.95x | 0.95x | | L4 | 184 | 2.17x | 1.08x | Closed loop, A100, TTFT of one request / throughput (8 requests in flight for gpt-oss, 4 for Qwen), median of 3 runs. Qwen3-8B is forced onto `TRITON_ATTN`; it defaults to FA2 on these GPUs, so that comparison is Triton against Triton. | model | 4k | 8k | 16k | 32k | |---|---|---|---|---| | gpt-oss-20b | −9 % / +6 % | −15 % / +13.5 % | −23 % / +26 % | −32.5 % / +43 % | | Qwen3-8B | −10.6 % / +4.5 % | −18 % / +10.7 % | −25.6 % / +19.7 % | −30 % / +28 % | Open loop, A100, ratio to main (Poisson arrivals, 70 % prompts of 256–2048 tokens, 30 % of 4096–12000, 128 output tokens; main and tile alternate between windows with identical arrivals; 150–300 requests per run, so p99 rests on 2–3 requests; bootstrap CIs over requests are optimistic): | workload | TTFT p50 / p95 / p99 | TPOT p50 / p95 / p99 | |---|---|---| | gpt-oss-20b, 2 req/s | 0.59 [0.52, 0.97] / 0.78 / 0.80 [0.75, 0.84] | 0.94 / 0.82 / 0.74 [0.59, 0.83] | | gpt-oss-20b, 2 req/s, other seed | 0.65 / 0.76 / 0.68 [0.59, 0.79] | 0.85 / 0.73 / 0.67 [0.62, 0.75] | | Qwen3-8B, 1.8 req/s | 0.84 / 0.84 / 0.91 [0.87, 0.92] | 0.94 / 0.99 [0.95, 1.00] / 0.96 [0.95, 0.98] | | gpt-oss-20b, 12 decoders at 16k + short requests, 3 req/s | 0.63 / 0.74 / 0.70 [0.65, 0.75] | 0.82 / 0.81 / 0.82 [0.82, 0.83] | Saturated closed loop (gpt-oss-20b, A100, 64 in flight, 240 mixed requests, about 51 s), req/s: | Triton cache | main | tile | |---|---|---| | warm | 4.718 | 4.818 (+2.1 %), TTFT p99 11.6 s → 10.5 s | | cold | 4.719 | 4.564 (−3.3 %), TTFT p99 11.6 s → 13.4 s | The tile adds about 96 Triton cache files (513 vs 417) and the cold run is slower than the warm one only with the tile, so I think the cold loss is first-use JIT (compile time not timed). Unified attention isn't in the startup JIT warmup, so a mixed workload pays a few seconds early on. On L4 with an empty cache the first 4100-token prefill was 0.2 s slower than main and the first 9000-token one 0.6 s (single runs). In my very first saturated run (default cache dir) the tile was 3.7 % slower even in its second server, which I couldn't explain; later runs on the same dir didn't repeat it. Adding the kernel to the JIT warmup would fix the cold start; I left that out. Numerics, Qwen3-4B, 24 prompts of 3k–12k tokens (182,291 positions), fp32 reference: | | top-1 disagreement | mean \|Δlogprob\| | |---|---|---| | main | 1.042 % | 0.0212 | | tile | 1.052 % (McNemar vs main p = 0.65) | 0.0213 | | FlashAttention-2 | 1.037 % | 0.0213 | RMS error: tile +0.0020 over main (95 % CI +0.0006 to +0.0036, about 4 %); FlashAttention-2 +0.0007 (CI includes 0). On 32 long prompts, 17 greedy continuations differ from main within 64 tokens (11 for FlashAttention-2). gpt-oss has no usable logprob comparison (its run-to-run noise on main is 0.05–0.19 nats with the Marlin MoE). GSM8K for gpt-oss-20b (5-shot, A100, earlier gate, tile used in 76 % of calls): 0.303 on both; it has little power (16–17 % invalid answers). Kernel output vs an fp32 reference: worst abs error 0.0104 for main and tile over 82 configs. `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` (default cudagraph mode), Qwen3-4B on L4, main vs tile: no errors or NaN, mean |Δlogprob| 0.0235–0.0262, the same size as the tile's own effect. ## Details - Gate (`_get_prefill_block_m`, host values only): 2048+ tokens, 6+ query blocks per sequence on average, 4+ programs per SM; bf16/fp16, head size 64–128, GQA ≤ 16; exactly sm80 or sm89; off under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`. Tile is 64 rows (head ≤ 64) or 128, 4 warps, 2 stages. Below 2048 tokens an earlier version was up to 19 % slower. No new setting, so no docs. - `unified_attention(..., prefill_tile=True)` is set only by `TritonAttentionImpl`. `ultraquant_attn.py`, `segmented_attention.py` and the ROCm callers keep the default launch. Also excluded: quantized KV, tensor-descriptor path, ALiBi, qq bias, mm-prefix, per-sequence or non-causal masks, rswa, chunked attention, fp8 output. Only plain causal attention (sliding window, sinks, softcap allowed) was tested. - sm86/sm87/sm90/sm100/sm12x keep the default (sm12x only has an early kernel run). - Not covered: a saturated open-loop run around 20 req/s (what the #20690 reviewer measured; mine reach 3 req/s, and L4 open loop used an earlier gate), H100/B200/sm12x, multi-GPU, Gemma-3 end to end, `FULL` graphs with the final code. - #52684 touches the same BLOCK_M lines (ROCm gfx1100/1151): one conflict region, keep both functions, the gates don't overlap. #60317: the kernel file merges cleanly, only the tests file needs a manual merge. The patch also conflicts textually with #62581, #61760, #61646, #61630, #60418, #51506 and #39018 (adjacent hunks, imports). If #37949 lands too, sm89 would get BLOCK_M 64 with a KV tile of 16, which I haven't measured. If #59878 lands, gpt-oss on sm80/sm89 may stop using this path. - No merged or open PR does this for CUDA (open, closed and merged PRs and issues searched with 13 query variants). - AI assistance: Claude (Anthropic) wrote the code, tests, benchmark scripts and this description. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

files.patch:
@@ -393,6 +393,7 @@ def ref_paged_attn(
     scale: float,
     sliding_window: int | None = None,
     soft_cap: float | None = None,
+    sinks: torch.Tensor | None = None,
 ) -> torch.Tensor:
     num_seqs = len(query_lens)
     block_tables = block_tables.cpu().numpy()
@@ -433,8 +434,13 @@ def ref_paged_attn(
         if soft_cap is not None and soft_cap > 0:
             attn = soft_cap * torch.tanh(attn / soft_cap)
         attn.masked_fill_(mask, float("-inf"))
-        attn = torch.softmax(attn, dim=-1).to(v.dtype)
-        out = torch.einsum("hqk,khd->qhd", attn, v)
+        if sinks is not None:
+            sink = sinks.float()[:, None, None].expand(-1, query_len, 1)
+            attn = torch.cat([attn, sink], dim=-1)
+        attn = torch.softmax(attn, dim=-1)
+        if sinks is not None:
+            attn = attn[..., :-1]
+        out = torch.einsum("hqk,khd->qhd", attn.to(v.dtype), v)
 
         outputs.append(out)
         start_idx += query_len
@@ -1251,3 +1257,198 @@ def test_softcap_does_not_overflow_on_large_scores() -> None:
     ref = soft_cap * torch.tanh(scores / soft_cap)
     assert torch.isfinite(out).all(), out
     torch.testing.assert_close(out, ref, atol=1e-3, rtol=1e-3)
+
+
+requires_prefill_tile_gpu = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_cuda()
+    or not (
+        current_platform.is_device_capability(80)
+        or current_platform.is_device_capability(89)
+    ),
+    reason="the larger prefill tile is only used on sm80 and sm89",
+)
+
+
+class _LaunchSpy:
+    """Records the keyword args of each kernel_unified_attention launch."""
+
+    def __init__(self, kernel):
+        self.kernel = kernel
+        self.launches: list[dict] = []
+
+    def __getitem__(self, grid):
+        launcher = self.kernel[grid]
+
+        def launch(*args, **kwargs):
+            self.launches.append(kwargs)
+            return launcher(*args, **kwargs)
+
+        return launch
+
+
+def _select_prefill_block_m(query_lens, num_heads, head_size, dtype=torch.bfloat16):
+    return attention._get_prefill_block_m(
+        head_size,
+        num_heads[0] // num_heads[1],
+        sum(query_lens),
+        len(query_lens),
+        num_heads[1],
+        dtype,
+    )
+
+
+@requires_prefill_tile_gpu
+def test_prefill_block_m_selection() -> None:
+    assert _select_prefill_block_m([8192], (64, 8), 64) == 64
+    assert _select_prefill_block_m([8192], (32, 8), 128) == 128
+    # Too few tokens, too few programs to fill the GPU, or decode-heavy.
+    assert _select_prefill_block_m([1024], (64, 8), 64) is None
+    assert _select_prefill_block_m([2048], (8, 8), 128) is None
+    assert _select_prefill_block_m([2048] + [1] * 255, (64, 8), 64) is None
+    # Unsupported head sizes, dtypes and GQA ratios.
+    assert _select_prefill_block_m([8192], (32, 8), 256) is None
+    assert _select_prefill_block_m([8192], (32, 8), 128, torch.float32) is None
+    assert _select_prefill_block_m([8192], (64, 2), 128) is None
+
+
+@requires_prefill_tile_gpu
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("dtype", "num_heads", "head_size", "use_sinks", "sliding_window", "soft_cap"),
+    [
+        (torch.bfloat16, (64, 8), 64, True, None, None),  # gpt-oss
+        (torch.bfloat16, (64, 8), 64, True, 128, None),  # gpt-oss sliding window
+        (torch.float16, (64, 8), 64, True, None, None),
+        (torch.bfloat16, (32, 8), 128, False, None, 50.0),
+        (torch.bfloat16, (56, 8), 128, False, None, None),  # 7 queries per KV head
+        (torch.bfloat16, (48, 4), 96, False, 128, None),  # 12 per KV head, padded
+        (torch.float16, (40, 8), 80, True, None, None),  # 5 per KV head, padded
+        (torch.bfloat16, (32, 16), 128, False, 1024, None),  # Gemma-3 27B
+        (torch.bfloat16, (16, 16), 128, False, None, None),  # MHA
+    ],
+)
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_triton_unified_attn_prefill_tile(
+    monkeypatch,
+    dtype: torch.dtype,
+    num_heads: tuple[int, int],
+    head_size: int,
+    use_sinks: bool,
+    sliding_window: int | None,
+    soft_cap: float | None,
+) -> None:
+    """The larger tile is launched only when opted in and matches the reference."""
+    seq_lens = [(3000, 3000), (1500, 3500), (800, 800)]
+    query_lens = [x[0] for x in seq_lens]
+    kv_lens = [x[1] for x in seq_lens]
+    torch.set_default_device(DEVICE_TYPE)
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    block_size, num_blocks = 16, 2048
+    num_query_heads, num_kv_heads = num_heads
+    scale = head_size**-0.5
+    query = torch.randn(sum(query_lens), num_query_heads, head_size, dtype=dtype)
+    key_cache = torch.randn(
+        num_blocks, block_size, num_kv_heads, head_size, dtype=dtype
+    )
+    value_cache = torch.randn_like(key_cache)
+    sinks = torch.randn(num_query_heads, dtype=torch.float32) if use_sinks else None
+    block_tables = torch.randint(
+        0, num_blocks, (len(seq_lens), 3500 // block_size + 1), dtype=torch.int32
+    )
+    spy = _LaunchSpy(attention.kernel_unified_attention)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(attention, "kernel_unified_attention", spy)
+    call = dict(
+        q=query,

+def _get_prefill_block_m(

+    num_tokens: int,
+    num_seqs: int,
+    num_kv_heads: int,

+) -> int | None:
+    """Larger BLOCK_M for prefill-heavy batches on sm80/sm89, else None.

+    The tile wastes rows on decode sequences, so it needs enough tokens, query
+    blocks per sequence and programs to fill the GPU.

+    if (
+        is_batch_invariant
+        or num_tokens < PREFILL_TILE_MIN_TOKENS

+            or current_platform.is_device_capability(89)

+    block_m = 64 if head_size <= 64 else 128
+    block_q = block_m // num_queries_per_kv

+        return None
+    num_programs = (num_tokens // block_q + num_seqs) * num_kv_heads
